Here's some tips from a very frugal guy who apparently needs Ron Swanson levels of liquor to get drunk:

  • Drinking is expensive and I am cheap. Kamchatka vodka is my miracle. Googling it gets very little, at most a piece from NPR. It's vodka made in Kentucky by Jim Bean, and depending on how close you live to Kentucky, it can be as cheap as $14/1.75L bottle or completely unavailable. That is ~39 shots, 2.8 shots per dollar spent. That is value!

  • Vodka goes in the freezer. Vodka goes in the freezer. I cannot tell you how many ignorant people I've seen with bottles of vodka in their liquor cabinet. Cheaper vodkas smell and taste like fucking nail polish remover, but the magic thing about vodka is that it loses most of its smell and taste when extremely cold! This is super-important for making mixed drinks, because it allows your mixers to completely disguise the taste of the vodka.

  • Spend like $20 on some mixers to have at home. Variety is important, but vodka mixes well with just about anything with taste, so you can pick just about whatever you want. I highly suggest generic diet sodas from your local grocery sodas if you're also worried about caloric intake. One shot is about 100 calories, so it can add up quick. Root beer, Mountain Dew (and Baha Blast!), lemon-lime soda+grenadine syrup, Orange Soda/Juice (with or without grenadine), strawberry lemonade, you name it. One shot, some ice, stir+you're good!

  • Beer is an acquired taste for most, just go to a bar and try some. That's about all I can say on that, I'm still not the biggest fan myself.

  • Get yourself a nice, big water bottle, fill it with ice and water. Every time you drink. Drink the everloving hell out of it, it'll save your life. It is that easy.

Most of my advice is about money. When I was 21, I was just getting out on my own. I had a job that paid pretty damn good. My rent, food and all my bills were covered by my first cheque, then the second one was all "profit". I bought all kinds of nice stuff. I have maybe a fraction of that stuff still 15 years later. I'd much rather have saved the money.

I'll keep it simple. Make a budget, and stick to it.

If you have, say, $500 left over after you're done buying groceries, paying off your bills and rent for the month, take $250 of that and put it into savings. Don't touch it. Get a savings account at another bank if you need to and "lose" the card. Never touch this money. The other $250, that's what you use for fun stuff. For going out with friends, for buying a TV, a car, whatever.

Don't carry a balance on credit cards. If you want something, save up until you can buy it. Then buy it on a credit card, and pay it off from the money you saved up. You'll build credit for when you want something big like a house or car you can't buy outright, but you won't get yourself into trouble with ridiculous interest payments.

Get in the habit of managing your money now while you're young and hopefully still debt free. Then you can concentrate on enjoying your life and having fun and not worrying about debt or borrowing off your parents or something.
